title: Perfect subtrees: countable sequence trees and continuum-many branches

based_on.title: Descriptive Set Theory, second edition
based_on.pages: 50–51 (Theorem 2A.1 and Corollary 2A.2); 57–61 (§2C, tree bodies and binary splitting; direct tree-only adaptation)

based_on.title: Searching for an analogue of ATR₀ in the Weihrauch lattice
based_on.pages: 2 (Perfect Tree Theorem); 18 (§6, perfect-tree definition and Definition 6.2); arXiv version 2, 2020-01-13

summary: A tree of finite natural-number sequences has countably many infinite paths or continuum many, with a largest perfect subtree accounting for all but countably many paths.
abstract: There are only countably many finite binary words, but their infinite paths correspond to all infinite sequences of zeros and ones. For any tree of finite sequences of natural numbers, an uncountable path set must have as many members as there are real numbers. This happens exactly when the tree contains a nonempty perfect subtree: above every node, one can find two extensions that disagree at some coordinate. Every such tree has a largest perfect subtree, and at most countably many of its paths lie outside that subtree.
